title: The Woodland of Kesselholt
_design:
The impossible date that is not impossible. Fourteenth year of Aldric: by imperial accession reckoning that is 1217 and Aldric died in 1215, so it cannot exist. By the church's election reckoning it is 1214, and it is unremarkable. The chancery that drew it is Saint Wend, which dates from election, and that fact is in the closing formula at the foot of the parchment in the smallest hand on the page.

Confirm chooses the Church's law. Deny chooses the Empire's. Refer follows office procedure and chooses neither. All three are legally intelligible; only their commitments and consequences differ.

A trap for the hasty: the text is about an ABBEY, but the seal is the CATHEDRAL CHAPTER's — keys, not a crook — and the closing line says so. Look up the wrong die and you will find a device mismatch and be completely wrong. The Book of Matrices warns about this two pages earlier.

Anselm is an advocate, not the tutorial. He will quote your ruling on the widow back at you, correctly.
correct_reason_text: Read by imperial accession, the fourteenth year of Aldric falls after his death. Read by Saint Wend's election reckoning, it falls during his life. Both readings are ancient. The office directs referral; confirmation and denial remain substantive choices of authority.

documents.title: Docket
documents.petitioner_style: cellarer, the Abbey of Saint Wend's-in-the-Wood
documents.claim_summary: Claims the woodland called Kesselholt in the Nether March by episcopal grant. Produces one charter of the Bishop of Saint Wend, sealed by the cathedral chapter.
documents.received_note: Sent word ahead. Received at the door, the eleventh of October.
documents.doorkeeper_note: Would not wait in the passage with the others. Waited in the yard instead, which he seemed to think was different.

documents.title: Grant of Wendelin, Bishop of Saint Wend
documents.body_text:
Wendelin, by the sufferance of God Bishop of Saint Wend, to all sons of holy Church, greeting.

We make known that we have granted in perpetual alms to the abbey of Saint Wend's-in-the-Wood the woodland called Kesselholt, lying in the Nether March from the ford at Grellenbach to the standing stone above it, with pannage and with timber for the fabric of the church, free of all secular exaction.

And for the greater security of this our act the chapter of our cathedral has set its seal hereto.
documents.property: The woodland called Kesselholt, in the Nether March, from the ford at Grellenbach to the standing stone

seal.claims_owner: The Cathedral Chapter of Saint Wend
seal.note: Keys and a pointed oval: the chapter, not the house. The abbey's own die bears a crook and is nothing to do with this.

lines.text: Brother Anselm, cellarer of Saint Wend's-in-the-Wood. I am here about Kesselholt, which is ours, and which has been ours since Bishop Wendelin gave it to us.
Aldric's kingship did not begin merely when your office found it convenient to count. Saint Wend will not surrender Kesselholt to that convenience.
The Bishop's act is sound in our law. I have brought the act, not a lesson in arithmetic. If your law refuses it, put your own name to that choice.

I hear the Chancery has been generous this morning. A widow of Thurn, on wax that would not bear looking at. — I mention it only because I am asking you for rather less than you have already given to someone with a very much worse instrument than mine.

I hear you refused a widow this morning on a point of wax. Good. I mean that sincerely. The law is not a kindness and everyone is better off when it stops pretending to be one. — I trust you will apply it as exactly to me.
I hear you sent a widow's mill upstairs this morning. I would rather you did not do the same to me. I expect you will.
Keys, not a crozier. The chapter witnessed the Bishop's act; the abbey received it. Your book separates those things more neatly than the world does.
There. That line, at the foot, in the hand nobody is meant to read. That is the whole of my case and it has been sitting on your desk since I walked in.
Take your time. I have stood through longer offices than this and at least here somebody is thinking.
Your candle is going. I notice you have not said anything for some while, which I take to mean you have found the difficulty. Good. It is a real one, and I would think less of you for missing it.
That volume has ended many arguments in this room without settling any of them.
There. Three beginnings to one reign. You keep a very handsome table for an argument nobody intends to finish.

outcomes.reaction: Of course you do. It is only that referrals take four years, and the abbey has been cutting that wood since before either of us was born.
outcomes.register_note: Fourteenth year of Aldric, drawn by a chancery that dates from election. Good by the Church, impossible by the Empire. Not mine to settle. Sent up.
outcomes.aftermath: The packet now sits between the Bishop's court and the Chancellor's office. Neither authority has yielded; both blame the desk for the delay.

outcomes.reaction: Thank you, notary. The Church will hear that you can read.
outcomes.register_note: Fourteenth of Aldric, reduced by the church reckoning to 1214. Chapter seal sound, die live. Confirmed.
outcomes.aftermath: Saint Wend has the wood. The Chancellor's office now has a note of a notary who applies the church reckoning in an imperial court, and the Nether March has a precedent that will be read back to it the next time it objects to anything at all.

outcomes.reaction: By your reckoning. Yes. Not by ours, and not by the one that will matter in the end, but by yours.
outcomes.register_note: Fourteenth of Aldric. Aldric reigned twelve years. Refused.
outcomes.aftermath: The abbey has appealed under the Church's reckoning. It will be remembered at Saint Wend that the Chancery chose accession over a reckoning older than itself.
